text:
Andy: Started an nsys run for the KV-prefetch regression on svc-13 — workload=chat-burst. Noticed a performance regression vs baseline, top GPU time looks dominated by launch overhead :thinking_face:

Jia: Can you paste the nsys summary / timeline? Even a short top-k kernels table helps.

Andy: Paste from nsys summary (trimmed):
```
Kernel, Calls, Total Time (ms), %
cuLaunchKernel, 18,432, 1220.3, 48.6%
fused_attention_forward, 6,120, 420.8, 16.8%
kv_prefetch_copy, 12,008, 210.1, 8.4%
softmax_kernel, 24,512, 130.7, 5.2%
memcpy_h2d, 9,004, 98.4, 3.9%
other_small_kernels, 75k, 210.2, 8.4%
```

Maria: cuLaunchKernel that high usually means lots of very small kernels being launched repeatedly. That fits with many tiny prefetch/copy ops. What's SM util / occupancy on fused_attention?

Andy: Occupancy snapshot from nvprof: fused_attention_forward avg SM util ~12%, warp efficiency ~65%, active warps low. So compute isn't saturating.

perf-bot: Top kernels by GPU time (auto-generated):
```
1) cuLaunchKernel - 48.6% - likely launch overhead / many tiny kernels
2) fused_attention_forward - 16.8% - low occupancy, potential suboptimal kernel variant
3) kv_prefetch_copy - 8.4% - memory-bandwidth dominated
```

Sam: Two hypotheses: (1) batching heuristic producing a lot of micro-batches -> many launches; (2) KV cache path is spawning extra small memcpy + kernel calls per request. Which batcher config?

Andy: Using dynamic batching with 8ms window + eager flush on tail. Historically increasing to 20ms amortized launch cost but increased latency p99. This regression looks like the selector chose a generic attention kernel after the last merge (didn't pick the quantized/fast variant for seq<=64).

Jia: If selector flipped to generic, fused_attention could be using a kernel with lower occupancy. Two immediate mitigations: prefer quantized kernel for seq<=64 in selector; or fuse prefetch+compute into a single kernel to avoid repeated cuLaunchKernel. Persistent kernel for prefetch is another option.

Maria: Also check the KV prefetch copy pattern: frequent small H2D copies show up in the summary. That explains the memcpy_h2d time and many cuLaunchKernel wrappers. Could be we introduced an extra memcpy per shard when trying to support partial KV loads.

Andy: Repro steps I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx -o out.nsys python serve_bench.py --model rwd-7b --seq 64 --batcher dynamic --clients 64
nsys stats out.nsys --report summary
```
Link to raw capture: https://perf.rwd/in/1851234567 (internal)

Sam: I'll run perfetto on a longer trace to get kernel timelines and look for launch spikes. I'll also try toggling selector to prefer the quantized kernel and re-run the same bench.

ops-bot: Canary deploy: selector=prefer_quantized applied to svc-13 (roll id c-5789) :rocket:

Jia: If canary looks good, let's add a CI smoke that runs a short nsys on a tiny synthetic workload and compares the top-10 kernels by cumulative GPU time to detect regressions automatically. That will catch selector regressions.

Andy: Action items:
- Sam: run perfetto + selector toggle, attach timeline and before/after nsys summaries (due: today)
- Maria: audit kernel selector diff in last PRs touching kernel routing (due: EOD)
- Jia: prototype CI nsys smoke test that asserts no >10% increase in cuLaunchKernel share (due: 1 week)

Sam: ACK :thumbsup:

Maria: ACK

Andy: Thanks team. I'll keep adding captures to the thread as we iterate.
